strategies.name: mean_reversion_scalp
element_inventory: PRECONDITION: trade only in-play stocks — a stock with a significant price range, doing high volume, often trading on a news catalyst or interesting technical pattern
PRECONDITION: require BOTH liquidity and volatility; reject random tickers with average volume and no catalyst (they provide choppiness and paper-cut losses)

PRECONDITION: identify a tight, well-defined intraday support/resistance level, ideally one that aligns on multiple timeframes and that other participants clearly see (tighter level = more defined risk)

PRECONDITION: read the tape before entering — watch how thick/thin the bids and offers are, look for disparity and which side is more aggressive, using the level-2 box (bids/offers) and the time-and-sales window

SETUP: mean-reversion scalp triggers after price stretches too far too fast into a level — step in when emotion peaks and order flow begins to shift (the shift is visible in the tape before it is obvious on the chart)

ENTRY TRIGGER (long at support): on a sharp DOWN move into support, wait for the moment where volume stalls and people stop hitting the bid (seller hesitation signifying a momentum turn), then take the offer and get long in front of the support level
STOP (long): use the bids at the support level as your protection (exit if the support gives way)
TARGET: capture the bounce we get off that level
VARIANT SUB-MECHANIC (short mirror at resistance): on a sharp UP move into a resistance level with large offers, fade it for the reversal — the mirror of the long-at-support entry

FILTER: prefer setups where the move into the level is sharp and big into really big size — massive bids at support (long) or large offers at resistance (short); the sharper and bigger the move into big bids/offers, the better the reversal scalp
SELECTION FILTER: take only a few high-quality opportunities where structure and order flow align; do not overtrade
coaching_notes: You are stepping in when emotion peaks and order flow begins to shift.
identify a key emotional level, confirm with the tape, and execute without hesitation
There is no room for distraction, and you're interpreting real-time information and making fast, calculated decisions.
The strategy is also cognitively demanding, requiring sustained focus over the course of a long day.
The margin for error is thin, and a single large mistake can erase many small gains.
Scalping is highly execution-dependent. Minor slippage, hesitation, or routing inefficiencies can eliminate or impair your expected value.
Transaction costs matter significantly because profit targets are small relative to frequency.
The more size you do, the more slippage you face, and in turn the more your edge degrades.
you tend to need to be glued to the desk during market hours
When you get the reps, you'll develop small positive edges, which, when repeated consistently, can compound meaningfully over time.
You do not need too many trades per day... often you can fall for the trap of not being selective enough and your win rate suffers.

strategies.name: continuation_breakout_scalp
element_inventory: PRECONDITION: trade only in-play stocks — significant price range, high volume, often on a news catalyst or interesting technical pattern
PRECONDITION: require BOTH liquidity and volatility; reject random tickers with average volume and no catalyst
PRECONDITION: identify a tight, clean, well-defined intraday support/resistance level, ideally aligning on multiple timeframes and clearly seen by other participants
PRECONDITION: read the tape (level-2 bids/offers box + time-and-sales) to confirm real-time order flow before entering
SETUP: continuation scalp triggers around breaks of clean support or resistance; aim to be the FIRST market participant to enter upon the break

CONSOLIDATION SUB-CONDITION: look for price consolidating under the level with multiple pushes into it, shallow pullbacks, and each dip finding buyers higher than the previous dip (attention building)

ORDER-FLOW CONFIRMATION: watch the large offer sitting at the level — check whether buyers are aggressively lifting into it, whether prints are going off repeatedly at the level, and whether the offer is refreshing (reappearing after partial fills) vs getting taken; require the offer size to begin shrinking then suddenly be gone
ENTRY (long): buy just above the resistance level on the break — e.g. $10.01 or $10.02; buy $50.01 if possible; buy $25 / $25.02 as the offer gets taken
ENTRY MECHANIC VARIANT: place a stop-limit buy order just above the offer/level to auto-enter the moment the whole offer is taken and resistance breaks

TARGET: scalp out on the emotional follow-through of traders scrambling to buy higher — kick it out roughly 10, 20, or even 30 cents higher (worked example: 5,000 shares kicked out ~10c higher at $25.10-$25.12 = ~$500)
STOP: place the stop right below the level; exit if price gets back below it (e.g. back below $50)

FILTER: require a strong, urgent breakout that bursts through the level with conviction and moves quickly in your favor; skip weak breakouts that drift through and stall (tape slows, sellers start hitting bids just above resistance, leading to failed breaks)
VARIANT SUB-MECHANIC (short mirror): applies symmetrically to breaks of clean support (breaks of clean support OR resistance)
SELECTION FILTER: take only a few high-quality opportunities where structure and order flow align; do not overtrade
coaching_notes: Your success in a continuation scalp trade will depend heavily on timing and confirmation from real-time order flow.
Strong breakouts feel urgent, and you want to see the stock burst through that level with conviction.

strategies.name: spread_making_scalp
element_inventory: PRECONDITION: use in a liquid 'spread' name where the stock is in relative equilibrium but thin — market participants who need urgency will cross the spread (pay the offer up there and hit the bid down there)
PRECONDITION: this is a foundational in-play/liquidity context — scalping thrives on liquidity; you need a real spread and volume for others to cross
ENTRY MECHANIC: provide the liquidity instead of taking it — place resting (passive) limit orders in spread names ahead of large bids or offers (acting like a market maker, not a momentum trader)
PROFIT MECHANIC: capture the difference between the spread as other participants cross and hit the bid / pay the offer; the edge is non-directional (does not come from predicting direction)

VARIANT SUB-MECHANIC (wide-spread event, Facebook-IPO-style): when there is an over-a-dollar spread with incredible volume going off on both sides, slam in huge bids only to just as quickly kick the offers/size out a point or two higher, repeating it again and again before the spread compresses (and the stock drifts lower)
SELECTION FILTER: take only a few high-quality opportunities where structure and order flow align; do not overtrade
coaching_notes: The edge here does not come from predicting direction. It comes from understanding market microstructure.
To do this well, you must really understand market microstructure of order types, queue priority, and hidden versus visible orders.
